headline: Russia's faster jet-powered attack drones are slipping past Ukrainian defences more often, and Kyiv is racing to field matching interceptors before winter.
score_reason: Important drone-war development, but the specific New York Times reporting was not read and the figures are 'reportedly'.
importance_line: People in Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities are affected as faster drones are harder to shoot down, but the interception figures are reported estimates and Ukraine's new interceptors are only entering service.
summary: AI News Desk, drawing on Forces News and the headline of a New York Times report of 15 Oct 2026 on the race to defend Kyiv, reports that Ukraine's interception rate has reportedly fallen from around 90% against older Shahed drones to below 60% against Russia's newer jet-powered Geran-4 and Geran-5. Ukraine is building jet-powered interceptors, four of which President Volodymyr Zelensky said in late September were entering service.
notes: Built from Forces News text; NYT article itself not read. Military story: counts toward the robot-war limit.
